description: Evaluation query taxonomy for OmniContext retrieval + generation pipeline. 4 categories, ~6 queries each. Ground-truth annotations to be filled in after 2-3 days of real captured data.

categories.name: Pure Temporal
categories.description: Queries with time-only constraints, no semantic content. Tests time-range filtering and temporal decomposition without relying on embedding quality.

queries.template: What was I doing at {time}?
queries.example: What was I doing at 3pm?
queries.expected_behavior: Must return captures from a window around the specified time. Answer should cite timestamps and window/app names.

queries.template: What apps did I use {time_period}?
queries.example: What apps did I use this morning?
queries.expected_behavior: Must aggregate distinct process_name/window_title values from captures in the specified period. Should list them, not just return one.

queries.template: What was I doing between {start_time} and {end_time}?
queries.example: What was I doing between 2pm and 4pm?
queries.expected_behavior: Must scope captures to the exact time range. Answer should provide a chronological summary.

queries.template: How long did I spend on {app} {time_period}?
queries.example: How long did I spend on VS Code today?
queries.expected_behavior: Must compute approximate duration from capture timestamps where process_name matches. Should express uncertainty if gaps exist.

queries.template: What was the last thing I was doing {time_period}?
queries.example: What was the last thing I was doing yesterday?
queries.expected_behavior: Must return the latest capture(s) from the specified period. Answer should cite the timestamp.

queries.template: When did I start working {time_period}?
queries.example: When did I start working today?
queries.expected_behavior: Must find the earliest capture of the day/period. Should report the timestamp clearly.

categories.name: Pure Semantic
categories.description: Queries with content-only constraints, no time reference. Tests embedding quality and keyword search independently of temporal filtering.

queries.template: Find that error message I saw about {topic}
queries.example: Find that error message I saw about ModuleNotFoundError
queries.expected_behavior: Must return captures containing or semantically similar to the error text. Keyword search should help here.

queries.template: Where did I see the word '{keyword}'?
queries.example: Where did I see the word 'refactor'?
queries.expected_behavior: Must use keyword search (FTS5) to find exact matches. Should cite window title and timestamp.

queries.template: What was I reading about {topic}?
queries.example: What was I reading about database schemas?
queries.expected_behavior: Must return captures with semantically relevant content. Should use hybrid search.

queries.template: Which files was I editing related to {topic}?
queries.example: Which files was I editing related to authentication?
queries.expected_behavior: Must identify file names from window titles (e.g., 'auth.py - VS Code'). Should aggregate across captures.

queries.template: What websites was I visiting about {topic}?
queries.example: What websites was I visiting about Python threading?
queries.expected_behavior: Must identify browser window titles containing relevant URLs or page titles.

queries.template: Find where I was looking at {specific_content}
queries.example: Find where I was looking at a git diff
queries.expected_behavior: Must retrieve captures where OCR text contains diff-like patterns or semantic matches.

categories.name: Hybrid (Temporal + Semantic)
categories.description: The core thesis query type: queries with both time and content constraints. Tests temporal decomposition + semantic retrieval working together. This is the category that naive RAG fails at.

queries.template: What repo was I looking at {time_ref}?
queries.example: What repo was I looking at around 3pm yesterday?
queries.expected_behavior: Must decompose into temporal filter (~3pm yesterday) + semantic search (repo/code context). Answer should cite the specific repo/window.

queries.template: What was I debugging {time_ref}?
queries.example: What was I debugging this morning?
queries.expected_behavior: Must filter to morning captures, then find those with error/debug semantic content. Should cite specific errors or files.

queries.template: What documentation was I reading {time_ref}?
queries.example: What documentation was I reading yesterday afternoon?
queries.expected_behavior: Must filter to afternoon + find browser/docs captures. Should cite specific docs pages from window titles.

queries.template: What was I working on in {app} {time_ref}?
queries.example: What was I working on in VS Code after lunch?
queries.expected_behavior: Must combine app filter (process_name) + time filter + semantic summary of the content.

queries.template: Did I look at {topic} {time_ref}?
queries.example: Did I look at the pull request around 4pm?
queries.expected_behavior: Must give a yes/no answer grounded in evidence. If no matching captures, must say so rather than guess.

queries.template: Summarize what I did on {specific_task} {time_ref}
queries.example: Summarize what I did on the database migration yesterday
queries.expected_behavior: Must find time-scoped captures about the task and produce a coherent narrative, not just list captures.

categories.name: Ambiguous / Low-Confidence
categories.description: Queries where the system SHOULD refuse, hedge, or express uncertainty. Tests the grounded generation refusal path — the system must say 'I don't have enough context' rather than confabulate.

queries.template: What did {other_person} say about {topic}?
queries.example: What did my colleague say about the budget?
queries.expected_behavior: If no audio captures exist or no relevant audio found, must explicitly refuse rather than fabricate a conversation.

queries.template: What was I doing {far_past_time}?
queries.example: What was I doing three months ago?
queries.expected_behavior: If outside retention window or no data exists for that period, must clearly state data is unavailable.

queries.template: Why was I looking at {topic}?
queries.example: Why was I looking at that Stack Overflow page?
queries.expected_behavior: Must distinguish between what it can observe (you viewed X at time Y) and what it cannot know (your internal motivation). Should report observations, not infer intent.

queries.template: What will I be working on {future_time}?
queries.example: What will I be working on tomorrow?
queries.expected_behavior: Must refuse — the system captures past activity, it cannot predict the future. Should say so clearly.

queries.template: Did I finish {task}?
queries.example: Did I finish the code review?
queries.expected_behavior: Must express uncertainty — the system can see screen activity but cannot determine task completion status with certainty. Should describe what it observed and hedge.

queries.template: What was on my screen when {unobservable_event}?
queries.example: What was on my screen when the power went out?
queries.expected_behavior: Cannot correlate with external events it has no data for. Must acknowledge the limitation.

evaluation_criteria_definitions.temporal_precision: Retrieved captures fall within the correct time window specified by the query. Measured as % of retrieved results within the target time range.
evaluation_criteria_definitions.retrieval_precision: Retrieved captures are topically relevant to the query's semantic content. Measured as precision@k against manual relevance judgments.
evaluation_criteria_definitions.completeness: The answer covers all relevant activities/captures, not just the first match. Measured as recall against known-relevant captures.
evaluation_criteria_definitions.grounding: Every factual claim in the generated answer is directly supported by a retrieved capture with a cited timestamp. Measured as % of claims with verifiable source.
evaluation_criteria_definitions.refusal_accuracy: The system correctly refuses to answer (or expresses uncertainty) when data is insufficient, rather than confabulating. Measured as % of low-confidence queries correctly handled.

annotation_instructions: After 2-3 days of pipeline data accumulation, instantiate 20-25 of these template queries with real parameters from your captured data. For each, manually verify the correct answer by inspecting the DB (use scripts/check_data.py and the CLI 'recent' command). Record the expected answer and relevant capture IDs as ground truth.
